data.description:
Chain link 2, "connects their own Stripe account" — server side only. Create the connected account with POST /v1/accounts (bare Standard-equivalent defaults), mint hosted onboarding links with POST /v1/account_links (type=account_onboarding), handle the return_url and refresh_url routes, and maintain the connected account's readiness state (charges_enabled plus outstanding requirements) on the record the data-model task defines.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-10 (Connect account creation and hosted onboarding) and C-11 (readiness state gating invoicing). Both IN under Rule 1.

DECISION CONTEXT. Every call goes through the custody-guard wrapper — no direct HTTP, no exceptions. The D1 spike (docs/strategy/spikes/spike-D1-freelancer-invoicing.md section 1) verified these exact primitives and that a bare POST /v1/accounts yields the Standard-equivalent controller properties we want: losses.payments=stripe, fees.payer=account, requirement_collection=stripe, stripe_dashboard.type=full. Stripe bears payment-loss liability, the freelancer pays Stripe's fees, and STRIPE COLLECTS KYC — we never see identity documents or bank details. That is precisely why building our own identity/document collection is OUT (row C-13, Rule 2), and it is a large part of why this architecture is constraint-7 clean.

Readiness matters because Stripe returns the user through return_url whether or not their requirements are complete. Invoicing an account that cannot charge breaks chain link 4, so the readiness flag maintained here is the gate the invoice task reads before finalizing.

VERIFICATION: request and response shapes validated against stripe-mock (free, no account); the return/refresh route logic and the readiness state machine unit-tested against fixture account and account.updated payloads. NAMED RESIDUAL, stated at creation rather than discovered at the review gate (milestone plan section 8.2, right-sizing test 3): stripe-mock is stateless and cannot exercise the real hosted-onboarding round trip, and it is not confirmed that Stripe test mode accepts http://localhost return/refresh URLs. Both are settled by the test-mode acceptance run, which is gated on the board's Stripe test-mode account. If localhost URLs turn out to be rejected, that acceptance task files a new board ask for local ingress — this task opens nothing and assumes no account exists.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the Connect screen and its states ledger (the onboarding-UI task); webhook receipt infrastructure (the webhook task — this task defines how an account.updated payload changes readiness, the webhook task delivers it); anything touching invoices.
data.title: D1 v1: Stripe Connect onboarding (server) — account, account_links, return/refresh, readiness

data.body: Pulled as trial lane A for AS-60's parallel-lanes trial (plan §4.1) and as the top D1 spine pull on its own merits — AS-38 and AS-39 are both done, so its dependencies are satisfied. Marcus implements: he carries the custody-guard context from AS-38 and the persistence context from AS-39, which is the whole D1 line. Owen plans as tech lead. Note for the planner: the plan's stated file scope becomes trial-config.json's allowed prefixes for lane A, so it must be explicit and file-level.

Plan written (tech lead: cto-owen). Route surface: POST /connect-stripe/start, GET /connect-stripe/return, GET /connect-stripe/refresh — all 303-redirect, identity via ?freelancer= seam until AS-40 (single replacement point, AS-40 OBLIGATION marked). Readiness ownership: one mapper lib/connect/readiness.js (AS-44 reuses it for account.updated); every write is a fresh-from-Stripe snapshot via connectedAccounts.updateReadiness; ready derivation stays AS-39's; return NEVER trusted as completion evidence. Declared file scope for the AS-60 lane lift (plan §2): allowed prefix set = [apps/invoicing/], nothing else — disjoint from apps/chat/ and tools/. Duplicate accounts stopped by row-check + UniqueViolation race convergence + stable Stripe idempotency key. 16 ACs, 5 falsification recipes, ~900 lines/12 files projected (tripwire justification + pre-agreed split line in §8).

lanes-trial: lane spawned — lane A, AS-60 T1, fan start 2026-09-02T06:54:38Z. Implementation runs as a sub-agent confined to .worktrees/AS-41; board writes are serialized through the orchestrator (agent:cto-owen) for the duration.

lanes-trial: lane killed — orchestrator terminated the lane A sub-agent at 2026-09-02T07:22Z, without warning it, per AS-60 plan §6.1.5. This is a deliberate resumability test, not a fault in the work.

State at kill, for whoever resumes: three commits on feat/AS-41-connect-onboarding — 8094944 (appBaseUrl config row), 58c017c (Connect onboarding service, routes, createApp deps), 26a8dfa (connect test suite, harness literal, README). Worktree .worktrees/AS-41 is CLEAN (no uncommitted residue). No as41 docker containers survive; the live containers on 8347/8348 were never touched. The lane's last action was tearing down its isolated compose project, and its final line reported that the as41 stripe-mock container had survived a first 'down' and it was retrying — the kill landed during that retry, so cleanup completed by luck rather than by the lane finishing it. Independently verified after the kill: no as41 containers remain.

The stage is NOT complete and the status deliberately stays in_progress — the board tells the truth about interrupted work. Unknown to the orchestrator: whether the suite passed, which acceptance criteria are met, and what remains. The resumer establishes that from the plan, the diff, and a fresh run; nothing here should be taken as a claim that the work is sound.

Deviation on the trial's own clock, recorded rather than hidden: the pre-committed kill point was first-observed-commit + one poll pass = 07:08:35Z. The actual kill was ~13.5 minutes late because the orchestrator's polling cadence was interrupted. The kill mechanism was exercised; the kill-TIMING datum is not a valid measurement of 'kill at first commit' and the spike result must say so rather than re-run for a cleaner number.
